sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Adam Preston, a housing development manager from the LGBT Foundation charity, says he regularly meets older members of the community in exactly that situation.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston is part of the team behind Kindred House, a first-of-its-kind LGBTQ+ social housing scheme for over-55s, set to open in Manchester next year.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: An artist's impression of what Kindred House will look like when it opens The scheme, a joint project with the local council, will provide 80 self-contained apartments and communal areas available to the local community.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston says he hopes the scheme will "trigger some conversations" about how to best support older LGBTQ+ people in the challenges they face.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Mindy and her wife Linda have been together for more than 30 years, but says they're often mistaken for sisters.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "She's 18 inches taller than me, I've got a Yorkshire accent and she's got a Northern Irish accent," Mindy says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think it's pretty obvious we weren't brought up in the same building." She believes part of that is often down to people presuming she is straight because of her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "There are different tribes of people in every age group, but when you get older, people start clumping you together with other stereotypes," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After divorcing her husband and coming out as lesbian, Mindy co-founded a lesbian commune in Hull before moving to Manchester On one occasion, while Mindy was in hospital after a stroke, a nurse referred to Linda as Mindy's husband.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She said it was not only "insulting", but made her consider what sort of training the staff might have had.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Spotlight on Ageing report says these sort of experiences can also have an impact on the support people receive.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Sarah Wilkinson, research and analysis manager at the Centre for Ageing Better, says after a "lifetime of homophobia and transphobia", older LGBTQ+ people now face the "additional, and overlapping, challenge of ageism".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report , external says older LGBTQ+ people are less likely to have children - someone born in 1950 would have been in their 50s by the time same-sex couples could legally adopt - and that they are more likely to be estranged from their families when compared to their heterosexual counterparts.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report also found more than half of gay and bisexual men aged 65 and above live alone, compared with less than a quarter of heterosexual men.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Bisexual women aged 50 to 64 are twice as likely as their heterosexual peers to live alone.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: It also suggests that only half of gay and bisexual men aged 50 and above definitely agree they would have someone to help them if they needed, 14 percentage points lower than heterosexual men of the same age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman Goodman, 75, came out as bisexual in his late 60s after the death of his wife Marilyn.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The couple never had children, and Norman now has no immediate family nearby to help him with things like hospital visits or housework.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: He says his support system comes in the form of his partner Tony, and a group of friends and neighbours he refers to as his "chosen family".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I'm lucky, I've got great friends and great neighbours, and I know I can knock on somebody's door day or night and I could get help," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman came out as bisexual when he was in his 60s and says he relies on "chosen family" to support him But despite having their support while he's relatively independent, Norman says he worries about the prospect of facing discrimination if he needs more formal care as he ages.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "Hopefully I will maintain and look after myself the best I can, but I've heard horror stories of gay people in nursing homes being treated terribly," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think nurses, doctors, carers should all be trained on how to look after LGBT people." It's the reason behind schemes like Manchester's Kindred House, which are not unusual in other parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There are similar projects in Spain, Sweden, Germany, the US and Canada, but in the UK they are few and far between.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: In 2021, the UK's first LGBTQ+ retirement community, Tonic, opened in London with 19 apartments for affordable rental or shared ownership.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The scheme attracted so much attention, later this year it is set to feature in a Netflix documentary telling the story of one of its first residents, Chek Min-Ong.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After 43 years together, Min, 77, and his late partner Tim, had discussed their plans for a future where one of them would live alone, as Tim's health deteriorated.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Min and his late partner Tim wanted to make sure they lived somewhere supportive when one of them passed away "Tim and I have always had this very open discussion, we wanted to know, when one of us is not here anymore, the other person will have a community and feel safe," Min says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: When Tim died five months after moving into Tonic, Min says his new-found community rallied around him.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It is what [Tim and I] always wanted, that we'd never have to explain ourselves," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "We'd never have to face a question and feel guilty about not telling the full story, or having to lie.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "You're just here, being yourself." While schemes like Kindred House and Tonic are welcomed by Mindy, Norman and Min, the Spotlight on Ageing report warns that, because the older LGBTQ+ population is growing, the demand for specialist services is expected to outstrip supply.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, the number of over-50s identifying as lesbian, gay or bisexual in the UK increased by around a third - from roughly 340,000 to almost 460,000.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There was a 4% rise in the number of heterosexual people aged 50 and above in the same period.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: These numbers are projected to continue to increase as the relatively larger younger generations of people identifying as LGBTQ+ age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston warns that without more schemes like Kindred House, and more training and awareness for those in other care settings, the ageing population may struggle to get proper support.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: For Mindy, who is part of a steering group advising on the plans, knowing there may be more options available in the future is reassuring.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's important that you can go, that you think, 'You know what, I could live there because I know the staffing, the ethics, the rules, everything about the place has been put together from an LGBTQ+ focus,'" she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "That's what we've been doing and it's something I'm really proud of being a part of."
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Hayley lost her job as a teaching assistant last October, after being told she was unfit to work Hayley Locksley was 11 years old when she started her periods and excruciating pain became part of her life.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley had her appendix removed because doctors thought that was the issue, until she was diagnosed with endometriosis After having her daughter, who is now aged seven, Hayley decided to pursue her dream of working with children again and became a special needs teaching assistant in a primary school four years ago.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "Having experienced first hand the impact endometriosis can have on your working life, I know just how difficult it can be.

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I really hope this isn't where the conversation ends.

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Firms are keen to explore how they can support women "without their careers being held back", in a "wider shift" towards helping improve health and wellbeing in the workplace, he adds.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley, Carla and Faye all say they hope employers can show more understanding of endometriosis in the future.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools and colleges in England will be required to recognise antisemitism as a distinct category of harm and take explicit action against it.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It means anti-Jewish hatred will be treated as a specific safeguarding risk rather than being dealt with through existing measures to stop racism and bullying.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The government has accepted all of the 27 recommendations made in the government-commissioned review including dedicated training for teachers and more consistent recording of incidents.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says The review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England was led by former Ofsted chief inspector Sir David Bell and presented to Parliament on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC it marked a "generational moment" to re-educate young people, among whom she said the issue of antisemitism was "particularly prevalent".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the House of Commons "teachers should not bring their own political views into the classroom" but they should not avoid discussing important topics.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review was launched following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025, in which two men were killed.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Separate reviews were also commissioned into antisemitism in healthcare and into public order and hate crime laws.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters .
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also recommends that the government sets up a type of hotline where school leaders can access immediate advice on tackling antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Bell, who is now vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, heard evidence from pupils, teachers, governors and parents across state and independent schools, as well as from community organisations.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: He told the BBC: "This is not just a report for Jewish children in Jewish schools.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This is for all children and young people in all schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We know that antisemitism crosses all boundaries." Earlier this month, the BBC was given rare access inside a Jewish school in Hertfordshire, where pupils and staff operate under tight security, amid heightened concerns about antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Spencer Lewis, the executive headteacher of Yavneh College, said that security was an "innate part" of his role.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "When you come in in the morning, there are high gates, high fences, lots of security cameras.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We have four full-time security staff.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: And it sort of just becomes part of what you do," he said.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "We think about it a lot." In response to the recommendations, the government will also encourage schools to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)'s working definition of antisemitism, although it cannot make it compulsory.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The definition is supported by mainstream Jewish organisations and has been adopted by 47 countries, including the UK, as well as most British universities.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: However, some of the IHRA definition's examples of antisemitic behaviour have proven controversial.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The Board of Deputies of British Jews said that adopting the IHRA definition would provide schools with a tool "to deepen understanding of contemporary antisemitism".

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.

sentences.text: The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Shrewsbury School has a campus in Bhopal in central India, while Wellington College has chosen to set up base in Pune, a western city that calls itself the "Oxford of the East" for its well-regarded universities and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Millfield, Queen Elizabeth's School and a few others are reportedly on their way with satellite campuses in the coming years.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: He said severe weather can bring heavy rainfall, rising water levels and flooding, with volunteers placed on standby to respond if needed.

sentences.article_title: The people on standby when a storm strikes

sentences.article_title: The people on standby when a storm strikes

sentences.text: "Being on standby, our volunteers are ready to mobilise at a short notice," he said.
sentences.article_title: The people on standby when a storm strikes

He said the risks associated with severe weather should not be underestimated, particularly around rivers and areas prone to flooding.

sentences.text: "Take weather warnings seriously, avoid flooded roads and paths.

sentences.article_title: The people on standby when a storm strikes

sentences.text: Twelve of the island's 16 breeding seabird species are on a list of greatest conservation concern Sewage being discharged into the sea and under-threat seabirds are among the challenges facing the Isle of Man after a decade as a UNESCO Biosphere, a report has said.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: The State of the Biosphere report looks back on the 10 years since the island became the world's first whole-nation Biosphere in 2016, in recognition of its thriving natural habitats from returning wildlife to new marine reserves.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: But it warns that while some wildlife is recovering, many species and habitats are still in long-term decline.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: It comes ahead of a UNESCO decision next summer on whether the island will keep its status.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: UNESCO (the United Nations' agency for education, science and culture) Biosphere status recognises places that balance protecting nature with supporting people, communities and the economy.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: The Isle of Man became the first entire country, including its surrounding seas, to be given the status, which is reviewed every 10 years.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: The Manx shearwaters population has succesfully recovered following a rat cull Among the successes of the Biosphere's first decade was the return of juniper, a native shrub that had been lost from the island.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: The last native plant on the island was dug up from Glen Auldyn in 1947 in an attempt to save it, but died soon afterwards.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: Since 2016, it has been replanted in the uplands, with surveys showing "encouraging survival and growth".
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: Meanwhile on the Calf of Man, controlling rats - referred to locally as "longtails" to avoid bad luck - has helped the Manx shearwater recover to about 1,500 breeding pairs.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: Nine new Marine Nature Reserves have been created since 2016, and together they now cover more than half the sea within three nautical miles of the coast.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: By the end of last year, 420 hectares of damaged peatland had also been restored.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: The Calf of Man, off the southern tip of the island, is an important breeding ground for seabirds A 2024 assessment found 48 of the 166 bird species regularly seen on the island were on the red list of greatest conservation concern.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: Another cause for concern was that monitoring has found declines in young salmon.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: The report also acknowledges sewage is still being discharged into the sea at Peel and in Garff, though work on a new treatment works for Peel began last year.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: It says Biosphere status is "not a claim that everything is working as it should", and that its credibility depends partly on being prepared to admit where it is not.
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: Biosphere Isle of Man chairman Jason Bissell said there was "much to celebrate from our first decade, and much still to do".
sentences.article_title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges

sentences.text: The report has been published alongside an exhibition at the Manx Museum entitled Jeihosphere, which tells the Biosphere's story through 10 objects, running until 28 February.

sentences.text: Conservation groups say England's black poplar trees are on the verge of extinction A project is aiming to help restore one of the UK's rare native trees across the Thames Valley using DNA testing.
sentences.article_title: Project to restore rare native trees with DNA testing

sentences.text: Conservation groups have warned numbers of black poplar trees have fallen due to decades of felling, land drainage and habitat loss.
sentences.article_title: Project to restore rare native trees with DNA testing

sentences.text: The Swindon to Oxford: Regenerating the Thames and Tributaries nature recovery programme is working with local conservation groups to regenerate the population along the River Thames and its flood plain.

sentences.text: Catrina Bass, from the Long Mead Foundation in Swindon, is involved in the project and said while the trees were "extraordinary survivors", there were just 50 recorded in Oxfordshire currently.

sentences.text: The project secured initial funding from West Oxfordshire District Council and the Vale of White Horse Council but is now aiming to raise £20,000 for the work, which involves DNA analysis of existing trees, propagating new cuttings and planting them in suitable sites.

sentences.text: Students at Ysgol Cemaes, on Anglesey, were able to put their questions to Frank Rubio on Wednesday, who is set to be part of the crew for the Artemis III mission .
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Rubio also spent more than a year aboard the International Space Station (ISS) after a fault with the spacecraft that was due to bring him and his fellow astronauts back to Earth.

sentences.text: During the virtual session, pupils asked him about his experiences of living and working in space, as well as the challenges and excitement of space travel.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Astronaut Frank Rubio was stranded on the ISS for 371 days This is not the first time pupils at the primary school have had the chance to speak with astronauts.
sentences.article_title: Pupils who designed a badge sent to space meet NASA astronaut

sentences.text: Earlier this year, they took part in a project to design a badge that was sent into space, later seeing it float in zero gravity aboard the ISS.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Spacecraft heading to Mars' moon Phobos lifts off from Japan A spacecraft has launched from Japan headed for Mars' moon Phobos, where it will attempt to grab some moondust and bring it back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: If it is successful, this will become the first time a sample has been returned from Mars or its moons to be analysed in laboratories here on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The spacecraft is scheduled to arrive at Phobos in August 2027.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It is hoped that the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission, which is led by the Japanese Space Agency, will solve the mystery of how Mars's moons formed.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Prof Sara Russell, from the Natural History Museum, who is the MMX mission's deputy for sample analysis, said: "There hasn't yet been a successful mission to go to Phobos and bring a bit back to Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "I think this is an incredibly ambitious and fun mission," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own Moon, and two around Mars, which are called Phobos and Deimos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Both of these are tiny - Phobos is about 20km (12 miles) across and Deimos is about 10km (six miles) across.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: They are also irregularly shaped, looking a bit like space potatoes.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos as it arrives in the Mars neighbourhood, and then will focus on Phobos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It plans to set down a small rover to explore the terrain, though this will be no easy feat.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Sara Russell says no one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "The moon itself doesn't have very much of its own gravity," she explained.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "But it's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity,  and that makes it much harder to get a rover onto the surface." Mars got its moons about 4.5bn years ago - but no one knows how they formed The rover will scout out a landing site so that the MMX spacecraft itself can later touch down on Phobos.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Once on the surface, it will deploy a robotic arm and two samplers to grab some moon dust.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: This material will be packed into a small capsule that will return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The amount of material that will come back is tiny - just 10g.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "It's a very small [amount] actually," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou, from Leicester University, who is working with the Japanese mission.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "However we can do several studies even on individual grains… You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So it's worth every gram," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The spacecraft will collect 10g of moon dust from the surface of Phobos Scientists believe the sample will finally shed light on the puzzle of where Mars's moons came from.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: There are two competing ideas.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Either a space rock smashed into Mars early in its history, and Phobos and Deimos were created from the debris.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Or the moons are two wandering asteroids from the outer Solar System, which were grabbed by the Red Planet's gravity.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results," said Sara Russell.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "It should be pretty much immediately obvious.. whether it's the product of this dramatic impact or whether it's a captured asteroid.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So we'll find that out really quickly." The team is also hoping there might be an extra bonus coming back to their labs.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "One of the really exciting things is that Phobos is so close to the Mars surface that whenever there's an impact into the Mars surface, little grains might actually become implanted into Phobos itself," said Russell.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: "And that means that the sample we get back may actually contain grains of Mars as well.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: So it can give us really direct information about the composition and history of Mars." Martian meteorites are rare - this one is on display at the Natural History Museum Bringing material from Mars back to Earth has long been an ambition of space scientists.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: The Nasa Perseverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since 2021, has been carefully collecting samples on Mars and storing them in canisters.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: But a second Nasa/ESA mission, called Mars Sample Return, that would have picked up and returned these canisters, has been effectively cancelled, after its funding was halted by the US Congress.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: China is planning its own sampling mission to Mars, set to launch in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: It will attempt to return Martian material to Earth in 2031.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: We do already have some fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth in the form of Martian meteorites.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: These are pieces of Mars that were blasted off the surface by asteroid strikes, and ended up being hurled towards the Earth.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Martian meteorites are extremely rare, but like all space rocks that fall to our planet, they become contaminated as soon as they get here, mixing with the air, dust, soil and water.
sentences.article_title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon

sentences.text: Scientists are so desperate to get their gloved hands on a direct sample from Mars and its moons because it would be pristine.

sentences.text: Firefighters said this summer's wildfires were the worst they had experienced Firefighters and the public were knowingly put at risk during this year's wildfires due to chronic underfunding, a union has said.
sentences.article_title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

sentences.text: Those working on the ground and in the South Wales control centre said the fires were relentless with injuries "commonplace" for crews.

sentences.text: The Fire Brigades Union (FBU) said firefighters were climbing hills in unsuitable boots and non-breathable layers used for house fires due to not having enough kit, and there was a "real risk to the public" if immediate action was not taken.

sentences.text: The Welsh government said it did not provide core funding but "recognise the concerns raised and are clear that we need to do all we can to reduce the risk of wildfires".

sentences.text: Sean Cayford said some injured firefighters from the wildfires are still not back at work Sean Cayford, a firefighter in Bridgend, said crews were told in mid-August that there were no pumps or fire appliances available across the brigade's entire region.

sentences.text: Trump's lawsuit - filed in Florida - accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave outside the Capitol on 6 January 2021.
sentences.article_title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit

sentences.article_title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit

sentences.article_title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit

sentences.text: In July, Trump's lawyers conceded they had no evidence that the documentary was available in the US on the BBC's BritBox subscription service - as they originally claimed - or on the BBC's website, BBC Select or through US broadcasters.
sentences.article_title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit

sentences.text: Trump ultimately agreed to drop the lawsuit against BBC Studios, the broadcaster's commercial arm, after the BBC argued that it had "no role in creating or producing the documentary".

sentences.text: Matilda The Musical is celebrating 15 years since its debut in London A musical that began life as a Christmas production in Stratford-upon-Avon has become one of the biggest theatre successes of the century as it celebrates 15 years in London's West End.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: Matilda The Musical, which is now the 10th longest-running musical in West End history, has been seen by more than 12 million people around the world, staged more than 10,000 performances and played in more than 100 cities.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: Composer and lyricist Tim Minchin said he was still amazed by the show's success.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: Based on Roald Dahl's classic children's novel, the production premiered at the Royal Shakespeare Company in Stratford-upon-Avon in 2010 before transferring to the West End the following year.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: Composer Tim Minchin and writer Dennis Kelly said they never expected the show's global success Written by Dennis Kelly, with music and lyrics by Minchin, the musical has gone on to win more than 100 international awards, including 25 for best musical.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: Kelly said neither of them expected the production to become a global phenomenon.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: "If we'd made a successful show at Stratford, we'd have been delighted," he said.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: It's mad." He attributed part of the show's enduring popularity to its message.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: "It says to kids, stand up for what's right.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: Be brave, reading and stories are freedom, your family is where you find it, love conquers all, little girls are powerful.

sentences.article_title: Call of Duty promises a return to form - but can it compete with GTA?

sentences.article_title: Call of Duty promises a return to form - but can it compete with GTA?

sentences.text: He says he's always thinking of ways for Call of Duty to leverage its position and "show up in culture in a really big and innovative way" to reach "as many people as possible".
sentences.article_title: Call of Duty promises a return to form - but can it compete with GTA?

sentences.article_title: Call of Duty promises a return to form - but can it compete with GTA?

sentences.article_title: Call of Duty promises a return to form - but can it compete with GTA?

sentences.text: "More people dusting off their Xbox or their PlayStation, starting to play for the first time, it gives an opportunity for more gamers to come in and play both of the games," says Bahl.

sentences.text: A mysterious caped figure has been helping the people of London.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Not dealing with the criminal hi-jinks of The Joker or Catwoman (thankfully), instead doing good deeds for others: paying for fuel at petrol stations, helping people across busy roads and even filling in potholes.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: These may not be the type of do-gooder acts that sell comic books, but London's Batman, as they are known, has already got 297k followers on TikTok and their posts have had more 2m likes since they first appeared at the end of September.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Despite the capital’s hero doing their best to make people’s days a little brighter, one question keeps hounding them: who are they?
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Can they be like Bruce and keep their identity secret, or will they soon be unmasked?
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Socials are awash with the theory that London's Batman is none other than Niko Omilana, known for posting prank videos on socials and as a contestant on the first series of The Celebrity Traitors .
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Niko appears to be the most popular candidate for London Batman’s secret identity as he has a reputation for pranks which take a lot of organisation and can involve handing out goods to people.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: In 2021, he opened a fake store in the city and gave away free smartphones to the public as his comment on what he saw as the high price of technology.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Niko posted a short video of himself on TikTok showing he was in the heart of New York, a move some people interpreted as him trying to prove he is not London’s Batman.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: That hasn’t stopped others trying to prove otherwise.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Comments on the post suggest it could have been pre-recorded as the theatre advertisements behind him don’t reflect the ones playing in the city at the moment, although this hasn’t been verified.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: TikTok user officialroyce1 posted that Niko’s video was meaningless as he could have flown to New York and back in the same day to cover his tracks.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: At the moment, there are lots of theories but absolutely no evidence that Niko is dressing up as a superhero and helping out in the community.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: A similar situation happened earlier this year when some posters on socials were convinced that the Liverpool rapper EsDeeKid was really the actor Timothee Chalamet in disguise .
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: This was later disproved after the theory went viral.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Until London’s Batman pulls back their mask to reveal their secret identity, we can’t say for sure.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Dave Hill, the lead guitarist for Slade, has named his album after a lane near his childhood home Slade star Dave Hill is set to release his debut solo album, paying homage to some of his old haunts in Wolverhampton.
sentences.article_title: Slade star Dave Hill's debut album honours city

sentences.text: Named Dirty Foot Lane, the 10-track album was named after a road near his childhood home and not far from where he lives today.
sentences.article_title: Slade star Dave Hill's debut album honours city

sentences.text: He collaborated with Noddy Holder's son, Django Holder, on the project, his first since the break-up of the band behind hits such as Merry Xmas Everybody.
sentences.article_title: Slade star Dave Hill's debut album honours city

sentences.text: "It's got a lot of depth to it, every one of those tracks is a true story about someone close or someone I've lost," he told BBC Radio WM.
sentences.article_title: Slade star Dave Hill's debut album honours city

sentences.text: Hill teamed up with Noddy Holder's son Django who produced the album The album blends rock, blues and folk, capturing the energy of Hill's live-performance roots alongside his personal journey, including struggles with mental health and the impact of the Covid-19 lockdowns.

sentences.text: African diaspora is finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage A new sound is taking Bristol's dancefloors by storm.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Driven by rolling log drums, syncopated rhythms and infectious melodies, amapiano and other electronic sounds from across the African diaspora are finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Behind these parties is a new generation of black promoters passionate about creating spaces where black people can hear their music, celebrate their cultures and feel like they belong.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But for some, building these spaces has also meant confronting the familiar challenge of finding spaces where black music and the communities around it are welcomed and not feared.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Unkle Mykel started hosting events to connect to different cultures Bristol-based promoter Unkle Mykel's journey into events began in his own back garden after he moved to Bristol in 2017.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: What started as garden barbecues gradually grew into a way of bringing people together, particularly members of Bristol's black, Asian and minority ethnic communities.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's about celebrating our cultures, bringing people into that fold and connecting," says the 32-year-old, who hosts Bristol Barbecue Family and The Aux Social.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Originally from Kenya, Mykel moved to the UK in 2005.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Since then, he has witnessed changes in the visibility of African music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There was no Afrobeats on the airwaves," he laughs, recalling his early years in the country, when he says Caribbean reggae, dancehall and soca were more prominent in the musical landscape he encountered.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Now, he sees the growing popularity of genres such as amapiano - a popular South African house music subgenre - as an opportunity to broaden the scene.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We don't need to pretend to be nobody else, we're just us.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: It just took a while to get there." DJ and promoter Khiah Lou runs amapiano event called Khaya Nights For 30-year-old DJ and promoter Khiah Lou, representation, she says, is central to her work.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Last year she launched Khaya Nights, an event dedicated to amapiano and other African Caribbean electronic dance music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Having performed internationally, she had seen how other cities had developed a wider range of events celebrating these sounds.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Bristol, she felt, was lagging behind.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Rather than wait for the scene to develop, Khiah decided to help build it herself.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "If we don't do it, who else is going to do it?" she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Young black people are starting to make a way for themselves because I don't think we have a choice." Khiah says these nights provide a place where people can connect with their identities and see their cultures reflected in the city around them.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "At first it seems like it's just a party, but it's so much more than that," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's really important for your own self-identity.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: If your community doesn't have events, where do you feel you can go?" "At first it seems like just a party, but it's so much more than that,' says Khiah Tazmin Samuels, who DJs as Azumei, shares those concerns about representation.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: As part of Rushtown, a black-led music collective, Tazmin wants to champion sounds and subcultures from across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "My main motivation for getting together with people and starting Rushtown came from seeing the lack of representation of black music that black people are currently listening to within the city," says Tazmin.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: She sees encouraging signs, with more black music-focused brands emerging in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But she believes the wider music industry has yet to recognise the value of what these promoters are building.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Tazmin says the wider music industry must recognise the value of black promoters But creating these spaces is not always straightforward.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Khiah says she has struggled to find venues willing to host nights aimed at black audiences.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Although she considers Bristol an inclusive city, her experience as a promoter has revealed a different side of its nightlife.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I've had some venue owners straight up tell me they're worried about having a black event," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I feel like black crowds are kind of met with fear, and that's really disheartening." Mykel describes similar tensions, saying that some venues are enthusiastic about hosting his events, only to face objections from people in the surrounding community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: The Bamboo Club opened in 1966 as a social hub for Bristol's Caribbean community The young promoters' experiences echo a much longer history of black Bristolians having to create their own spaces for music and social life.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Many black people were turned away from existing clubs and bars in Bristol during the 1960s, which led to the creation of  "blues parties", un-licensed house parties where people danced to genres such as ska, reggae and rocksteady.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: In 1966, Tony Bullimore and his Jamaican-born wife Lalel, opened the Bamboo Club, which served as a cultural lifeline for the city's Caribbean community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Glen Crooks, 70, who used to perform at the Bamboo Club when he was younger, remembers "sneaking in" with his friends when they were young.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was the only place that we could have," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Especially all the Caribbean people could go and really have a good time." Rushtown aims to champion a variety of music genres from the African diaspora Marti Burgess, who has been a co-owner of the nightclub Lakota since 1994, says although attitudes have changed over the years, some prejudices remain.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There is a long history of treating a predominantly black audience as a concern, rather than recognising the audience, creativity and business that a promoter is bringing," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "They should not have to keep proving that black audiences are welcome or commercially worthwhile." Growing up, Marti was surrounded by music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Her parents went to the blues clubs and attended the Bamboo Club when it hosted artists such as Bob Marley, Desmond Dekker and Johnny Nash.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was through listening to the adults' conversations that I came to understand how much those spaces had grown out of exclusion from mainstream venues," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Amid drumming and dancing, Boateng Bismark James leads 13 worshippers, nine men and four women, in prayer for drivers and passengers travelling to destinations across Ghana.
